name: Project scaffolding and CI
description:
Create the repository, both app projects, and a build that runs itself. Comes AFTER F001's verification, deliberately — see below.

CURRENT STATE: /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter is EMPTY and is NOT a git repository. Depends on F007 (tools installed) and should follow F001 (platform facts established).

WHY THIS COMES AFTER VERIFICATION, not before: F001/T002 asks whether blocking an SMS on Android requires becoming the default SMS app. If it does, Android SMS filtering as specified is not deliverable at acceptable scope, and the Android project is a materially different shape — possibly a whole messaging application. Scaffolding a project for a shape we have not confirmed is the wrong order. F001/T001's measured limit likewise feeds F002's expander, which is the first real core work after this feature.

SCOPE:
- git init, repository layout. One repo holding core plus both apps, or separate repos — undecided, and it determines how UniFFI bindings and packaged datasets flow between them.
- Cargo workspace and the core crate skeleton, building and testing on the host. F002 is pure logic with no platform dependency, so its tests must run with no device or simulator.
- Xcode project with THREE targets: host app, Call Directory extension, SMS filter extension. Both extensions link the same core and run under tight memory limits, so the core's binary size and load cost are tracked build outputs from day one, not later discoveries.
- Android Gradle project linking the same core through JNI via cargo-ndk.
- CI: build the core per target, run its tests on the host, generate bindings, build both apps, run F003's dataset converter and fail the build on its validation errors.
- Shared conventions: formatting, linting, test layout, dependency policy. Agreed once here rather than argued per pull request.

TWO CONVENTIONS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THEY LOOK:
- UniFFI bindings are GENERATED by the build and never committed. Checked-in bindings drift from the core silently and surface as a runtime failure on one platform only.
- Packaged datasets are build outputs too. A checked-in dataset defeats R5's versioning, and a silently truncated one makes rules stop matching with no error anywhere.

APPLE SIGNING, current constraint: free personal-team provisioning, 7-day certificates, own devices only, no App Groups. The real app needs an App Group to share rules between host and extensions, so a paid account becomes a hard prerequisite before F004 is functional.
workDone: Repository created on main with the Rust core building and testing on the host, and both app skeletons linking that core through UniFFI. iOS has three targets (app, Call Directory extension, message filter extension) and is verified running on a real iPhone displaying values read across the FFI. Android builds an APK carrying the core for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64. tools/build-ios.sh and tools/build-android.sh perform the whole per-platform pipeline including binding generation and size reporting.
workRemaining: T009 — CI and shared conventions: build all seven targets, host tests, binding generation, both app builds, dataset validation failing the build, formatting/linting/test-layout/dependency policy, binary size tracking, and a possible lint enforcing the no-country-specific-code rule. Separately open: running the Kotlin call on real Android hardware, which has never been executed.
